page: Microsoft Azure DS11_v2 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the DSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor configuration includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 14.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 29 GB volume, and there are no integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the DS11_v2 sits primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall into the weak and poor categories respectively. Similarly, data processing tasks such as software compilation with Clang and ray tracing register in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. However, the system demonstrates moderate memory subsystem efficiency, with the PassMark memory score achieving an average rating, and text generation for a small 135M parameter LLM model also reaching average performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the DS11_v2 offers a high memory allocation relative to its low vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive CPU processing. The low compute performance and weak database operations benchmark suggest it is less suitable for high-throughput transactional databases or heavy web serving. Instead, the instance is best suited for lightweight background utilities, small-scale caching, basic text processing, or low-demand development and testing environments where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed.
